title: Our Eyes Look to the Lord Our God

questions.question: To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:1 (ESV): "To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens!"

questions.question: Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:2 (ESV): "Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master,"

questions.question: As the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:2 (ESV): "...as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her mistress,"

questions.question: So our eyes look to the Lord our God, till he has mercy upon whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:2 (ESV): "...till he has mercy upon us."

questions.question: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us, for we have had more than enough of what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:3 (ESV): "...for we have had more than enough of contempt."

questions.question: Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:4 (ESV): "Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease,"

questions.question: And of the contempt of the what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:4 (ESV): "...and of the contempt of the proud."

questions.question: This Psalm is a Song of what?
Who are enthroned in the heavens according to verse 1?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:1 (ESV): "...O you who are enthroned in the heavens!"

questions.question: What do the eyes of the servants look to?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:2 (ESV): "...look to the hand of their master,"

questions.question: How many times does the phrase "have mercy upon us" appear in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:3 (ESV): "Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy upon us,"

questions.question: What is the "soul" sated with in verse 4?
Who are the ones "at ease" in verse 4?
questions.explanation: Psalm 123:4 implies the scorn comes from those at ease.

questions.question: The imagery of looking to the hand signifies what?
What type of prayer is this Psalm?
questions.explanation: The "us" language and the plea for mercy suggest a community in distress.

key_verse_text: Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the Lord our God, till he has mercy upon us.
